extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscientists and neuroimaging researchers studying humor, language, and electrophysiology (MEG/EEG)
extracted.subtask_description: Spatiotemporal investigation of neural dynamics underlying joke appreciation using anatomically constrained MEG (aMEG), contrasting funny, congruous, and incongruous punch-line types and relating them to N400/P600-like processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage model of humor comprehension (incongruity detection then resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Punch lines are appreciated as funny in two stages: (1) the punch line is perceived as incongruous with the setup, and (2) further consideration establishes a deeper coherence with the preceding context (e.g., detection of a ‘twist’ and frame shifting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amusement may result when a 'twist' in the meaning is successfully incorporated into the preceding context—that is, when the initial incongruity is resolved by reinterpreting or 'frame shifting' (Coulson, 2001). The study explicitly manipulates surprise/ambiguity and coherence to probe these stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: N400 / N400m as index of lexical–semantic access and incongruity detection
rubrics_metrics.description: A negative deflection peaking at ~400 ms (N400) is evoked by potentially meaningful material and interpreted as an attempt to access and integrate a semantic representation into a current context; N400m (magnetic equivalent) reflects the same process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N400 is sensitive to lexical, semantic, and mnemonic aspects and reflects semantic fit with world knowledge. In this study, incongruous endings evoke the largest N400m, consistent with integration difficulty; funny punch lines evoked the smallest N400m during the initial lexical–semantic stage, consistent with 'surface congruity' with the setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: P600 / late positivity as index of ambiguity detection and integrative resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: A late positivity often follows the N400 (P600) and is observed to semantic ambiguities that need to be resolved; it is sensitive to sentence plausibility, structure, and discourse complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the context of humor comprehension, the P600-like protracted positivity (700–1,150 ms) may reflect resolving the incongruity of the punch line and establishing coherence with the preceding context, possibly indexing combinatorial analysis and/or conflict-monitoring (Kuperberg, 2007; Kolk & Chwilla, 2007). Funny punch lines elicited a larger P600-like response in this study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left-lateralized temporo-prefrontal involvement in initial semantic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Left anterior temporal and left inferior prefrontal regions contribute to the lexical–semantic access embodied by the N400m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These left frontotemporal areas are most active during the 350–550 ms 'lexical–semantic stage' and show greatest activity to incongruous endings (largest N400m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right dorsolateral prefrontal sensitivity to 'funniness' (resolution/integration stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (RPF) shows stronger activity to funny punch lines during the ambiguity detection and global integration stage (~700–1,150 ms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This area is interpreted as uniquely sensitive to deriving global coherence and alternative meanings that produce humor; right prefrontal regions may lead extended temporo-frontal networks in establishing distant unexpected creative coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and operationalization of stimulus conditions: funny, congruous, incongruous
rubrics_metrics.description: Three ending types: 'funny' — unexpected but makes sense (surface congruity and deep resolution); 'congruous' — logical, not surprising, coherent with setup; 'incongruous' — surprising and nonsensical, difficult to integrate with the setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stimuli were categorized a priori and validated by independent raters for plausibility (goodness of fit) and surprise/expectancy; funny endings were unexpected yet judged plausible, incongruous were rated as not making sense, congruous were expected and plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus selection and matching criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes selected to be funny but not offensive (ethnic/gender) and to have short punch lines (many are puns); congruous and incongruous variants created by replacing punch lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punch lines equated across conditions for number of words, syllables, letters, and (when possible) corpus frequency. Ratings from independent raters on plausibility and surprise guided selection. The entire stimulus list provided as supplemental Appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral rating procedure and inclusion of trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects rated each sentence set as 'funny' or 'not funny' after a response cue; averages and analyses used only trials free of artifacts and that were rated correctly as funny or not funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioral measures reported (percentages and reaction times). Inclusion criterion: trials had to be artifact-free and correctly rated to contribute to condition-based averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation timing to emulate naturalistic joke delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Words presented individually (240-ms duration, 390 ms onset-to-onset); punch line presented 2.1 s after last word of question; response cue 1.83 s after punch line onset; next sentence 2.4 s later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing intended to emulate everyday joke telling where a brief suspenseful pause occurs between setup and punch line, inducing anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant selection and control variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects: healthy, right-handed male participants aged 22–30, medication-free, no neurological impairments; consent obtained; response hand switched mid-experiment for counterbalancing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handedness and gender are relevant variables in prior ERP studies; here participants were all right-handed males to control variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEG/EEG data acquisition standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Whole-head MEG with 204 channels (102 pairs planar gradiometers) recorded continuously at 600 Hz sampling and 0.1–200 Hz filtering; simultaneous EEG at Fz, Cz, Pz; electrooculogram recorded; electrode impedance <5 kΩ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition-based averages constructed from artifact-free trials, bandpass filtered at 0.5–20 Hz before averaging. These acquisition parameters and artifact controls are applied to obtain reliable ERPs and MEG waveforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomically constrained MEG (aMEG) source localization approach
rubrics_metrics.description: aMEG combines whole-head high-density MEG with individual high-resolution structural MRI cortical reconstructions to constrain inverse solutions; cortical surface subsampled to ~2,500 dipole locations per hemisphere; noise-normalized minimum norm inverse used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-registration of MEG with MRI used digitized fiducials and Polhemus system; forward solution computed with a boundary element model; no a priori assumption on dipole orientation; noise estimates from 300-ms prestimulus window used for normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic statistical parametric maps (dSPMs) and noise-normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Noise-normalized average estimates of local current dipole power are transformed into dSPMs that match the F distribution under the null hypothesis, producing 'brain movies' across time points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noise-normalization improves point-spread uniformity across cortex (~20 mm). dSPMs display statistical tests that, at a latency/location, test the null hypothesis that activity does not differ from baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source localization uncertainty and interpretive caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Source localization is inherently uncertain due to spread of signal, limited sensor sampling, overlapping sources, and inverse solution assumptions; metrics such as 'crosstalk' (~17%) and 'point-spread' quantify uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors caution that inverse assumptions (allowed generation locations, focal vs distributed sources, synchrony) influence results; spatial resolution improves with more sensors and subjects; interpret localization with these limitations in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROI selection and group-based fixed-effects averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: ROIs chosen based on overall group-average estimated activity; same set of group-based ROIs used for all subjects, translated across surfaces with automatic spherical morphing, analogous to fixed-effects fMRI averaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach was blind to individual activations; estimated dipole strengths averaged across cortical points in an ROI and across time points in selected time windows for within-subjects ANOVA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis windows and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Two latency windows defined for analysis: 350–550 ms ('lexical–semantic analysis') and 700–1,150 ms ('ambiguity detection and global integration'); within-subjects ANOVA used to compare conditions for each ROI and time window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses were conservative (control for intersubject variability) and planned comparisons were used; reported p values were not corrected for multiple comparisons because comparisons were planned, but the authors advise prudence in interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing and normalization steps for inverse estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Dipole strength power estimated at each cortical location every 5 ms using linear estimation minimum norm; local current dipole power normalized by noise power from prestimulus window to produce statistical maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization transforms power maps into statistical significance maps and makes the point-spread function relatively uniform across cortex, enabling comparisons across latencies and subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral/experimental control reporting (accuracy and RT reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report of behavioral consistency with categorizations: percent of jokes rated 'funny' and percent of congruous/incongruous rated 'not funny'; reaction times measured from response cue and compared across conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speed of reactions not expected to differ because measured from response cue rather than punch lines; behavioral validation supports neural contrasts.
